rods.name: Bamboo Rod

rods.name: Driftwood Staff
rods.description: Heavy and slow, but the wide tip gives you a more forgiving catch window.

rods.name: Fiberglass Rod
rods.description: Lighter than bamboo with a wider tip. Gives you a more forgiving catch window.

rods.name: Reef Guard
rods.description: Responsive and fast. Bites come a little quicker than the baseline.

rods.name: Telescoping Rod
rods.description: Extends deep. Something about the length draws rarer fish to the surface.

rods.name: Moonwood Staff
rods.description: Carved from driftwood blessed by a full moon. Quicker bites and a wider catch window.

rods.name: Graphite Rod
rods.description: Lightweight and stiff. Noticeably quicker bites.

rods.name: Navigator's Rod
rods.description: A well-balanced deep-sea rod. Good speed and a wider catch zone.

rods.name: Carbon Rod
rods.description: Precision-engineered for quick, snappy bites.

rods.name: Deep Diver
rods.description: Built for the abyss. Fast bites and a wide catch window.

rods.name: Legendary Rod
rods.description: Forged from the mast of a sunken galleon. Faster bites, and the rarest fish cannot resist.

rods.name: Twin-Strike
rods.description: Two hooks on one line. When luck strikes, they both bite.

rods.name: Second Wind
rods.description: Stubborn rod. When you miss, sometimes it refuses to let go.

rods.name: Millionaire's Rod
rods.description: Hand-rolled in gold leaf. Every catch brings two.

rods.name: YOLO Rod
rods.description: Roll the dice every cast for a 100-fish haul — and the odds climb the shallower you fish. The rest of the time? Just a regular catch.

rods.name: Completionist Rod
rods.description: Forged from the soul of every species in the sea. A master's tool on its own, and a vessel besides: fit up to three rods you own into it to carry their gifts, and re-forge whenever you like.

rods.name: Treasure Rod
rods.description: Lures the deep’s lost hoards — doubles your chance of hooking a crate.

rods.name: Perfect Rod
rods.description: Rewards flawless form — perfect catches grant double XP, and it scales with your streak.

rods.name: Galaxy Rod
rods.description: Spun from cosmic thread. After any catch, open a wormhole and reroll it into a different fish from the same waters — fortune or folly, you take what surfaces.

rods.name: Lightsaber Rod
rods.description: A blade of pure energy. Fish are drawn to the light — most casts bite almost the instant your line touches the water.

rods.name: Yoon's Locked-In Rod
rods.description: Rewards a hot hand. Chain perfect catches to LOCK IN: 3 in a row quickens your bites, 5 lands a triple haul on every catch, and 10 quickens them further into a rare-fish frenzy. Hold the streak to keep it all — one miss and you start over.

baits.name: Worms

baits.name: Night Crawler
baits.description: Fish bite 15% faster. Widens your catch zone by 4° — a bigger catch zone means more room to land the needle.

baits.name: Angler's Formula
baits.description: Fish bite 35% faster. Widens your catch zone by 8° — a bigger catch zone means more room to land the needle.

baits.name: Luminous Lure
baits.description: Fish bite 40% faster and the catch zone widens by 10°. Earned from expeditions and bounties, or bought with Fathoms in the Locker. Something ancient stirs when it glows.
baits.hint: Something ancient stirs when it glows.

baits.name: Golden Lure
baits.description: Fish bite 45% faster. Widens your catch zone by 10°. The finest lure in existence — a rare drop, or bought with Fathoms in the Locker. The oldest things in the deep rise for its shine.
baits.hint: The oldest things in the deep rise for its shine.

shinyMessages: A golden {fish}. The kind of catch sailors carve into the hull.
{fish} of gold under your hand. Captain, this is one in a thousand.
Sailors tell tales of gold-scaled ones. Tonight you've held one.
A gilded {fish} — the sea's own coin. Mount it, or part with it for a king's haul.
Gold-scaled and impossible. Even the old captains only saw one of these.
A {fish} drawn up in solid gold. The dockside won't believe you without proof.
Worth more than a hold of common haul, and rarer than the stories about it.
The crew has gone quiet. None of them have ever seen a golden one before.
A golden {fish}. Every captain hopes for this once in a career.
The deep turned a {fish} to gold tonight, and gave it to you.

lines.text: ...*Megalodon.*
The last one. The one all the others were only ever leading up to.
All six. In a single pair of hands.
Do you have any notion what you have just finished building?
Years I stood at that black water, and it would not open for me. Not one inch. And you...
You were exactly what it was waiting for. Exactly what *I* was waiting for.
Never mind. Old rivals get sentimental.
Go on. Enjoy your wall of monsters.
The long-neck. *Plesiosaurus.* I have watched that thing take a rig and swim off like it felt nothing.
It let you land it. Sat in your hands like it decided to.
The deep does not just decide. Not for most of us.
Hm. Go on, then.
*Dunkleosteus.* A jaw like a ship's prow, older than the first keel that ever cut this water.
I hooked it once. It took my line and left me the story. That is all it has ever left anyone.
It handed you the whole fish. I would sit a while with why.
...or do not. Just keep pulling them up.
*Mosasaurus.* The sea-dragon every old chart drew a hard border around.
Turns out that border was the only honest ink on the page.
Every soul who chased these is a name cut in stone now. Every one but you.
That was never luck. Luck drowned a long way back. You are something the water wants.
The *Basilosaurus.* It swam this water before there was a single soul alive to fear it.
I have wanted to look one of these in the eye my whole life. Never once got the chance.
And here it lies on your deck, dripping like a market cod.
Sits wrong, does it not. ...Good. It ought to.
*Shastasaurus.* The largest thing that ever drew breath in salt water, and it is on your hook.
The others all swore these were stories. Easier than admitting they were out of reach.
They were never out of yours. The deep keeps handing you what it kept from me.
...from everyone. So keep pulling, captain. I mean to see just how far those hands of yours can reach.

residents.name: Sandy Sole

residents.name: Nell Pollack

residents.name: Hattie Ling

residents.name: Sim Dory
residents.line: Dark water pays. Hold out, coin in, and mind how you go back up.

residents.name: Bess Skate
residents.line: Furthest scale on the chart. Whatever you have got, I will take it.

note.title: A chart scrap, weighted with a stone
note.body: Fish are worth more the further out you catch them. The lanes price by how far you hauled it, not by what it is, so a common thing from the deep can beat a rare thing from the shallows.

note.title: A note nailed to the post
note.body: The water goes in rings and each ring wants a better captain than the last. Open Waters asks Fishing 15, the Deep asks 30, the Abyss asks 50 and the Ancient Deep asks 75. Nothing out there is hidden. It is only far.

note.title: A page torn from a logbook
note.body: The shoals that shimmer are worth steering for. Three of them sit on this sea at any time, each one helping with something different, and they pick up and move about every ten minutes. Sail into one and it will tell you what it is doing for you.

note.title: A bottle, corked with wax
note.body: Watch the light. This sea runs a full turn from dawn back to dawn in about three quarters of an hour, and the mark up in the corner tells you where in it you are. Some out here only trade after dark.

note.title: A note in a tin, still dry
note.body: If the haul out here is wearing you down, it is the boat and not you. The Shipyard sells hull, and hull is the difference between a crossing you dread and one you do not think about. Stock rides at three hundred. It does not have to.

note.title: The last page of the Wreckwood log
note.body:
Day fifty one. We have eaten the bait and the cook has stopped pretending otherwise. He says the water here is older than the water at home and I have given up arguing.

Whoever finds this: the fishing is better nearer the shelf. Do not take our heading.

note.title: Scratched into the post itself
note.body:
We put in here to wait out the dark and the dark did not end. Counted eleven turns of it. On the ninth the youngest asked whether we had sailed past the morning and none of us had an answer worth giving her.

We are going on. The hold is empty and going back is further than going on.

note.title: A bundle of pages, tied with line
note.body:
The Farthing went down four lengths off this rock in water so still you could read by it. No squall. No reason. She simply stopped being a boat.

We pulled six of her crew out and left with them. If you are anchored here reading this, do not anchor here.

note.title: One line, cut deep
note.body:
We were nineteen days past the last rock anybody had named and we named this one anyway, because a thing with a name is a thing you can come back to.

We did not come back to it. Somebody should.

bottleFragments: Third week without sight of land. The bosun has started naming the waves. We let him, because the alternative is silence.
To whoever finds this: the water east of here is colder than it has any business being, and the fish know it before you do.
We are out of salt, out of rope and nearly out of argument. Turning for home at first light, which the mate says was also true yesterday.
Caught something last night that we put straight back. Nobody has said what it was and nobody is going to.
The captain has been sounding the same patch for six days. She will not say what she is listening for.
If you are reading this we did not make it back, and I would rather you had the paper than the sea did.
Ran the whole night on a wind that came from nowhere and went nowhere. Made forty leagues and could not tell you which way.
The lamp went out at the worst hour and we sat in the dark and were, for a while, extremely honest with one another.
Note for the next crew: she pulls to port under full sail and there is no fixing it, only knowing it.
We buried a friend at the deep edge today. The water there does not take things down so much as accept them.
Nine days of flat calm. I have read this ship’s entire library, which is one book, four times.
Saw a light out past the last band and put about hard. Some things you leave for a braver season.
The cook swears the current runs backwards past the shelf. He is right, and none of us will admit it to his face.
Half the hold is water and the other half is fish, and at this point I could not tell you which is winning.
Whoever left the last bottle: we found it, we read it, and it helped. Passing the favor on.
Made port with nothing to show and every one of us still aboard. Some voyages you count that as the catch.
